newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton prices fall as transport strike ends.
newsitem.headline: India cotton prices fall as transport strike ends.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Thursday fell as a 10-day-old nationwide transport strike ending giving rise to more supplies coming into the market, dealers said.
Mill demand remained slow but stockists were booking profit as transport unions on Wednesday called off their strike that has crippled the economy.
Unions in Bombay said however they were continuing the protest until the Maharashtra state government withdrew local increases in vehicle and sales tax.
"Last week arrivals remained very slow due to the strike by the truckers but now supplies will pick up as transport operators will ply again," one broker said.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by 10/15 rupees at 900/950 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned fell by 10/25 rupees at 1,550/1,660 rupees per maund. F-414 fell by 20 rupees at 1,890/1,920 rupees per maund. Gujarat cotton on the other hand remained steady at the improved level amid shortage of superior varieties as well as limited activity.
Sentiments for the average and medium cotton remained subdued at the close on reports that Indian cotton yarn exporters were facing competition from neighbouring Pakistan.
Dealers said this competition may curtail export of yarn from India which in turn would lower the offtake of cotton by spinning mills.
